thread:
lee: heads-up — we're getting a cluster of client reconnect loops on streaming (SSE) after the proxy returns 204 on resume. clients do a full reauth+resume and we see duplicate billing hits. console sampling shows only 1% of these sessions are being traced, so it's hard to correlate.

nina: can you dump a short trace and the proxy logs?

lee: paste logs below:
```
[proxy] 2026-03-19T14:03:12Z INFO resume id=abc123 upstream=204 route=eu-west-1
[client] 2026-03-19T14:03:12Z WARN resume failed status=204 treated_as=error
[billing] 2026-03-19T14:03:13Z INFO charge tenant=team-x tokens=42 request_id=xyz789
[client] 2026-03-19T14:03:13Z INFO reconnect start auth=full
```
lee: key is the client lib interprets 204 as a terminal resume failure and falls back to full auth. that then triggers a second server-side charge.

rachel: @lee do we know which rollout touched resume semantics? I think there was a small proxy flag flip last night.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: resume-backoff-behavior=reject_on_204 -> started 2026-03-19T02:00Z by rachel (canary 10% -> 100%).

kevin: ugh. that flag was meant to make resume strict for a different proxy implementation. looks like older clients expect 204 -> success (noop). new behavior treats 204 as error.

nina: can we confirm which client versions are affected? stack traces?

lee: quick sample from access logs: most failing user agents are mobile-sdk/2.1.x and web-sdk/3.0.0-rc. server-side resume responders still return 204 when session has no new data. proxy change made 204 mean "resume rejected".

kevin: two problems: (1) UX/console shows only 1% telemetry sampling so we can't stitch traces to billing IDs. (2) billing is not idempotent for resume fallback path. both need quick fixes.

rachel: proposal: rollback the flag to restore previous semantics (accept 204 as ok for resume). then follow-up: add a strict metric to console (sample all resume failures for 5m) and a small billing de-dupe guard for 1 minute on resume->reauth path. thoughts?

lee: I support rollback. can we also add a visible console snackbar for ongoing rollouts that change resume semantics? this caused a silent behavioral change w/o clear signals.

nina: ops: if we rollback now, we need a canary stage and a quick regression test for idempotent billing. I can add a smoke that simulates resume->204->reauth sequence.

kevin: for medium-term: we should standardize resume status codes in the protocol doc and add a compatibility matrix per client SDK. also console should surface "behavior-changing" flags in rollout UI.

rachel: action items:
- rachel: initiate rollback of resume-backoff-behavior flag (canary 5% -> 100%) — target ETA 10m
- nina: add smoke test + enable 100% tracing for resume outcomes for 5m (console metric) — ETA 15m
- lee: gather a 5-min list of affected billing request_ids and open a billing-ops ticket for de-dupe — ETA 30m
- kevin: update protocol doc PR to include exact resume semantics and a compatibility note for older SDKs — ETA EOD

lee: small interim mitigation: we can set proxy to translate 204 -> 204_ok header so clients that look for a relaxed header will continue. but that's hacky. prefer rollback.

rachel: starting rollback now. ping me if you see any spike in other errors. :thumbsup:

lee: thanks all. after rollback I'll re-run the sampled traces and post correlation.

nina: will also add a temporary console alert to show "resume semantics changed" so support can triage incoming tickets.

kevin: after this, can we add an automated test that asserts billing idempotency for resume fallback? I don't want to chase charges later.

lee: yep, will draft that test tomorrow.

rachel: rollback complete at 2026-03-19T14:10Z. monitoring now.

lee: monitoring looks cleaner already — reconnect loops dropping by ~90%. will follow up with billing hits list in the ticket.

deploy-bot: note: resume-backoff-behavior flag reverted by rachel at 2026-03-19T14:10Z.

nina: closing temporary 100% trace in 5 minutes. keep an eye on console sampling windows.

lee: thanks — filing postmortem draft now.
